data.title: Uyun Al-Jiwa: Literary Heritage, Historical Landmarks Enrich Qassim's Tourism Landscape
data.content:
Uyun Al-Jiwa, November 22, 2026, SPA -- Uyun Al-Jiwa Governorate in Qassim Region combines literary heritage, historical landmarks, traditional architecture, and agricultural attractions, offering diverse tourism experiences rooted in local culture.
    Located approximately 42 kilometers northwest of Buraidah, the governorate had 29,178 residents according to the Saudi Census 2022.
    Al-Jiwa is associated with the pre-Islamic poet Antarah bin Shaddad, who mentioned it in his celebrated Mu'allaqa (poem). Local folklore links Antarah and Abla to Antarah Rock and Al-Naslaa Rock, the latter distinguished by its cone shape and ancient carvings of ibexes and camels.
    The 6,000-square-meter heritage town preserves traditional Najdi buildings, including Uyun Al-Jiwa Mosque, built from mud and stone, and Al-Mashaqiq, ancient rock-cut wells and water channels, some exceeding 100 meters.
    Historic markets include Souq Al-Majlis and the longstanding Monday Market, which attracts visitors from across the region.
    The governorate is renowned for date production, particularly Sukkari, Barhi, and Wannana varieties, alongside fruits and vegetables.
    Other attractions include Mount Al-Marqab, historically used for observation, King Salman Park, the Public Park, and Al-Watan Garden.
    -- SPA
